title: Sleep On The Floor
tonal_center: C minor with E-flat major light at declaration moments
production_thesis: A small-room testimony begins almost unprotected, gains old-school freestyle motion as survival takes over, blooms into lush 90s R&B harmony on the declarations, and ends with a current-generation rap-sung refusal.

rhythm: deep modern sub-bass under the hook
transitions: tape-stop half beat before the final declaration

sections.name: cold_open
sections.production: Window rattle, streetlamp hum, one organ chord, no full drums. The first inhale is audible before the lyric.
sections.purpose: Put the listener inside the room before the beat arrives.

sections.name: verse_1
sections.production: Late kick enters under line two; low electro pulse appears only at phrase endings; hi-hats remain imperfect and sparse.
sections.harmony: One low smoky double appears on 'woman I'm supposed to be.'

sections.name: declaration_1
sections.production: Dry clap and syncopated freestyle bass lock together; horns answer the final stressed word without copying a known melody.
sections.harmony: Three-part bloom: low third, center lead, upper fourth; airy octave appears only on the tail.
sections.purpose: The first moment survival becomes power.

sections.name: verse_2
sections.production: Remove the bright synths. Let the 808 and room texture carry the weight. Bajo-sexto-like syncopation may appear as an original muted-guitar gesture, not a genre costume.
sections.harmony: No harmony on the brother line. One low shadow enters after the emotional crack.

sections.name: bridge
sections.production: Drums fall to sub pulse and finger snap. Broken phrases sit behind the beat, then tighten into a short rhythmic vow.
sections.purpose: Move from memory into decision using a current-generation phrasing switch.

sections.name: final_declaration
sections.production: Full late-pocket drums, modern sub, electro bass counterline, organ, restrained horns, and a short synth-bell answer. No celebratory gloss.
sections.harmony: Five Luzaria layers: lead, tight unison, low third, upper sixth, airy octave accent. Every layer keeps the same formant identity.
sections.purpose: Make 'I refuse to lose' feel earned, not motivational.

sections.name: outro
sections.production: Beat drops away. A dry whispered echo of the refusal remains with the window hum and one unresolved organ extension.
sections.purpose: End close to the listener, not on a giant pop finish.

mix_rules.lead: Dry and close, centered, with short dark plate and selective eighth-note delay on phrase tails.
mix_rules.harmonies: Wider than the lead but below it; slight timing differences create 90s warmth without losing intelligibility.
mix_rules.low_end: Electro pulse occupies upper bass; modern sub owns the bottom octave; trap 808 cannot mask the vocal chest range.
mix_rules.master: 48kHz/24-bit, warm transient shape, no crushed vocal dynamics, final loudness chosen after lyric intelligibility passes.

blocked_drift: turning testimony into a dance novelty
